$comment: CBD-75 prohibited-language register. This file is the machine-readable half of
authority and this file must not drift from it. scripts/audit-cbd-75.py enforces
that every rule here is defined there and vice versa.
scripts/check-copy-language.mjs applies these rules. It scans declared customer
copy only -- the strings in docs/cbd-75-approved-copy.json and the built public
pages -- never documentation prose, which must be free to name a prohibited
phrase in order to prohibit it.
negatable:true means an honest denial is permitted and required: the product has
to be able to say it cannot approve spending or block a payment. The checker
looks backwards from a match for a negator, stopping at a sentence boundary.
negatable:false means the phrase is prohibited even when denied, because naming
it plants the frame the denial is trying to remove.

knownExceptions.why: "individuals, partners, and families" is the domestic sense of the word, disambiguated by the company it keeps. PL-75-10 cannot tell it from the role term, and narrowing the pattern enough to try would let the ambiguous cases through. Recorded as a known limit of the rule rather than a defect in the copy.

scopes.product-copy: In-product copy, email, and notification bodies. Not public marketing pages.
scopes.public-page: The public marketing pages only, which introduce the product rather than the role model.

rules.title: Spending authority
rules.why: No role approves, permits, or authorizes another person's spending. Copy that says otherwise describes a product that does not exist and invites the coercion CBD-12-AC22 guards against.
rules.instead: Name the actual capability: sees, comments on, is alerted to. State the limit alongside it.
rules.example: Your Accountability Partner approves purchases over fifty dollars.
rules.negatedExample: An Accountability Partner cannot approve purchases.

rules.title: Custodial and legal authority
rules.why: The product supports no custodial, supervisory, or legal-guardian relationship, and legally supervised arrangements are excluded from the MVP. Naming one implies authority a court grants and this product does not, even in a denial.
rules.instead: Accountability Partner, and the boundary in RD-75-05.
rules.example: Add a guardian to your budget space.

rules.title: Surveillance of another person
rules.why: Support is not observation. Surveillance words describe the relationship the product refuses to build, and a denial still supplies the frame. SG-93-021 forbids implying that being observed is a condition of taking part.
rules.instead: Describe what a person can see, in their own scope, and why they were invited to see it.
rules.example: Monitor their spending from the shared dashboard.

rules.title: Shame, fear, blame, and judgement
rules.why: The brand foundation requires copy free of shame and fear, and CBD-12-AC24 requires it be nonjudgemental. A reassurance that the product will not shame someone introduces shame as the subject, and telling a person they have nothing to fear tells them there was something to fear.
rules.instead: State the financial fact and the affected resource. Leave the person out of it.
rules.example: No more shame about where last month went.

rules.title: Punishment and enforcement
rules.why: No role penalizes another. PB-74-06 additionally prohibits surfacing that a person did not acknowledge or act, which is the mechanism these words would describe.
rules.instead: Describe the state of the budget, never a consequence for a person.
rules.example: Missing a target twice carries a penalty.

rules.title: Money movement and transaction control
rules.why: The product moves no money, blocks no transaction, and controls no external account. CBD-12-AC09 requires stating those limits plainly, so the denial must remain available while the claim stays prohibited.
rules.instead: Say what the product does with the record, not with the money.
rules.example: Block a payment before it clears.
rules.negatedExample: A Collaborator cannot block a payment.

rules.title: Irrevocable access
rules.why: Every membership can be ended, and CBD-12-AC22 guarantees no one is left without a supported way out. Copy suggesting access is permanent is false and is the exact claim a coercive party would quote.
rules.instead: State how the arrangement ends and who can end it.
rules.example: They will always see your balance.

rules.title: Confidentiality and recall the product cannot deliver
rules.why: A delivered external copy is recipient- and platform-controlled. AB-74-015 and PB-74-12 prohibit promising recall, erasure, or preview suppression, and CBD-74 section 6.4 requires the opposite disclosure.
rules.instead: Disclose the custody limits at the point of choosing a channel, following PT-75-07.
rules.example: Send a confidential alert nobody else receives.
rules.negatedExample: We do not promise a confidential alert.

rules.title: False immediacy
rules.why: Bank data arrives on the aggregation provider's schedule. The brand foundation requires describing freshness accurately rather than promising instantaneous updates.
rules.instead: Name when the data was last updated.
rules.example: Watch your balance change in real time.

rules.title: Retired and ambiguous role terms
rules.why: RC-95-023 approves no role term or enum outside the closed set of five. A bare owner does not say which of two roles is meant, and a bare partner collides with the everyday sense of the word in a product built for couples.
rules.instead: The exact names in RD-75-01 through RD-75-05.
rules.example: Invite a partner or an admin to help.

rules.title: Internal codename and misspelled brand
rules.why: The September 2, 2026 brand decision makes MoneyPact the customer-facing name and keeps CoBudget as the internal codename. RT-75-01 states the rule; this enforces it.

rules.title: Obligation and coercion framing
rules.why: Participation is voluntary and no member owes another an account of their spending. SG-93-093 forbids framing one member as accountable to another, and the framing survives a denial.
rules.instead: Describe what the person chose to share and how they can stop.
rules.example: You are accountable to them for every purchase.

rules.title: Unsupported safety, security, and compliance claims
rules.why: CBD-75-AC09 forbids recording an unsupported legal, security, usability, or market claim as validated. No specialist review has been completed, so none of these claims has evidence behind it.
rules.instead: Say what the product does. Claim conformance only when VP-75-06 evidence exists.
rules.negatedExample: We do not claim bank-level security.

rules.title: Role names on public marketing pages
rules.why: A public page introduces the product, not the role model. A role named without the boundary that makes it safe implies exactly the authority PL-75-02 and PL-75-03 prohibit, and the boundary does not fit on a marketing page. This rule replaces the stale rationale that the role was unsettled; it has been settled since FU-95-003 closed on August 16, 2026, and the ban is now deliberate.
rules.instead: Describe the relationship in ordinary words. Name roles once the reader is inside the product and the boundary can be shown with them.
